Description: A group of ink-inscribed pottery sherds (ostraca) found in a guardroom at Lachish, mostly letters from a field officer named Hoshaiah to his commander Yaush. Written in rapid Hebrew script, they report watching for signal fires from Azekah because Lachish could no longer see them.
BiblicalSignificance: Jeremiah records that Lachish and Azekah were the last fortified cities holding out as Babylon closed in, and these letters appear to catch that very moment. One letter even echoes complaints made against Jeremiah. They bring the fall of Jerusalem out of abstraction and into the handwriting of frightened, faithful men.
Interpretations: Scholars agree these are genuine military letters from Judah’s final years; debate concerns a few readings and the identity of some named officials.
